title: Variables with Symbol Table: Assignment and Lookup
description: The parser adds a symbol table (self.vars dict) for variables. F looks up names; statement handles 'print E;' and 'NAME = E;' assignments. Two test programs show sequential assignment and the single-scope limitation.

steps.description: Parser.__init__ tokenizes with regex matching numbers, names, or non-whitespace chars. pos tracks position. self.vars = {} is the symbol table mapping names to values.
peek returns current token or None. match consumes token if it matches expected value.
E and T methods unchanged from Model 1: E handles +/-, T handles */, both left-associative loops calling the next level down.
F method: if token is (, parses E then matches ). Otherwise matches the token: if digits returns int, else looks up name in self.vars (returns value or raises KeyError).
match(token) consumes the name token. isdigit() distinguishes numbers from names. Variable lookup is a single dict access: self.vars[token].

steps.question: In 'x = x + 4', which x is read and which is written?
steps.answer: The right side reads the old x from self.vars; the left side writes the new value to self.vars[x] after evaluating the right side.

steps.description: statement: peeks first token, matches it. If 'print', evaluates E and prints. Else treats token as a name, matches '=', evaluates E, stores in self.vars[name], then matches ';'.
First test: x=3; x=x+4; print x*2; -> x becomes 7, prints 14.
Second test: x=1; y=2; x=10; print x+y; print x+y; -> prints 12, 12. Single dict means x=10 overwrites x=1; no block scope to restore outer value.
